canonical.title: Escape hatches for the leftovers: Wine, a VM, passthrough, or just keep the partition

parent.title: Throwing away Windows: a replacement plan for an actual installed-software inventory

siblings.title: Your .NET + SQL Server stack on Linux: what actually replaces what
siblings.summary: Rider replaces Visual Studio + ReSharper on Linux at the cost of the WinForms/WPF designers; SQL Server itself moves cleanly to a container, but SSMS has no Linux successor now that Azure Data Studio is dead.

siblings.title: Microsoft 365 on Linux in 2026: what you actually lose
siblings.summary: Office, Teams and mail are a tolerable compromise on Linux in 2026; OneDrive sync and OneNote are the two places where the gap is real.

siblings.title: The utility belt: per-tool Linux verdicts for a Windows power user (2026)
siblings.summary: Per-tool verdicts for the Windows-only utilities in an actual installed-software inventory: most transfer cleanly, AutoHotkey and Power Automate Desktop have no single answer, and Wayland is the variable that decides the rest.

siblings.title: Multi-monitor, window management and the desktop shell: replacing DisplayFusion, Fences, FancyZones and X-Rite on Linux
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma 6.7 is the only Linux desktop that replaces most of DisplayFusion and FancyZones natively; Fences has no real equivalent and the X-Rite workflow becomes ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL plus a per-screen ICC profile.

siblings.title: Gaming after the switch: your library survives, the NVIDIA App does not
siblings.summary: Both installed games run under Proton — Planetfall is Gold/Deck-Playable and Fall Guys' EAC is Linux-enabled — so the only hard loss is the NVIDIA App and Game Bar tooling layer, which becomes environment variables plus MangoHud and GPU Screen Recorder.

siblings.title: Legion hardware, peripherals and the two corporate VPNs on Linux
siblings.summary: Neither corporate VPN blocks the switch — Harmony SASE ships an official Linux agent and WatchGuard is reachable with plain OpenVPN; the real losses are QuantumENGINE, Dolby, XTU and Lenovo's AI/Space bloat.

sources.title: WineHQ
sources.claim: Wine is a compatibility layer for running Windows applications on Linux; 11.0 is the stable branch in 2026 and AppDB is the compatibility database to check first.

sources.title: WineHQ AppDB Rating Definitions
sources.claim: WineHQ publishes Platinum/Gold/Silver/Bronze/Garbage rating definitions, so an app's viability can be triaged before committing effort.

sources.title: Broadcom: VMware Desktop Hypervisor licensing
sources.claim: VMware Workstation Pro is free for personal, educational and commercial use, downloadable from Broadcom without a licence key, and runs on Linux.

sources.title: Lan Tian: Intel+NVIDIA Optimus laptop passthrough
sources.claim: On a muxless Optimus laptop, dGPU passthrough caps guest resolution at 640x480, NVIDIA drivers will not form Optimus with a virtual iGPU, and setup requires custom UEFI, vBIOS extraction and ACPI patching.

sources.title: bottlesdevs/Bottles
sources.claim: Bottles is the mainstream GUI for managing Wine prefixes for non-game Windows applications.

sources.title: Linux Mint forums: Visual Studio under Wine
sources.claim: Visual Studio 2022 cannot be run usefully under Wine; even if installed it works very poorly with large amounts of missing functionality.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: licensing Windows virtual instances
sources.claim: A Windows licence covers one instance on one device, physical or virtual; additional virtual instances require additional licences.

sources.title: WilhelmZA/ssms-on-wine
sources.claim: SSMS 20 runs under Wine 11 with patches: connect, Object Explorer, Query Editor and Server Properties work, while Azure connection types, SSAS/SSRS/SSIS designers, Always On dialogs and the Tuning Advisor do not.

sources.title: winapps-org/winapps
sources.claim: WinApps uses FreeRDP to render Windows applications from a VM or remote Windows box as seamless windows alongside Linux apps.

sources.title: Computerworld: Windows 365 pricing
sources.claim: Microsoft cut Windows 365 Cloud PC prices by 20% on 1 May 2026, to $28-56 per user per month, excluding Microsoft 365 productivity apps.

sources.title: Are We Anti-Cheat Yet?
sources.claim: Fall Guys is rated Running (not Supported) and requires Proton GE or Experimental; 55% of the 1,166 tracked anti-cheat games are broken on Linux.

sources.title: lutris/lutris
sources.claim: Lutris is the game-oriented Wine/Proton runner and prefix manager.

sources.title: CodeWeavers: how CrossOver licences work
sources.claim: CrossOver+ costs $74, renews at $34/yr for continued support and updates, and CrossOver Life is $494.

sources.title: It's FOSS: sharing files with GNOME Boxes
sources.claim: Clipboard and folder sharing with a Windows guest requires manually installing SPICE guest tools, plus phodav/spice-webdavd in the guest for guest-to-host file sharing.

sources.title: NVIDIA developer forums: laptop dGPU in QEMU/KVM
sources.claim: A Lenovo Legion 5 Pro RTX 3060M passthrough attempt initialised video but Windows did not recognise the device as RTX 3060 hardware and NVIDIA's drivers refused it.

sources.title: Arch Wiki: QEMU guest graphics acceleration
sources.claim: virtio-gpu 3D acceleration is mature for Linux guests, while a fully functional OpenGL/Direct3D driver for Windows guests is still work in progress.

sources.title: Bottles (official site)
sources.claim: Official site for Bottles, the Wine prefix manager recommended as the first hatch.

sources.title: CodeWeavers (CrossOver)
sources.claim: Vendor of CrossOver, a commercially supported Wine distribution.
